Block

Block class and related utilities for Plot3D structured grids.

A Block represents a single structured grid block in a multi-block Plot3D mesh. Each block stores 3-D coordinate arrays X, Y, Z with shape (IMAX, JMAX, KMAX) and provides basic geometric operations (scale, shift, cylindrical conversion, cell volume computation).

The module also provides compute_gcd() and reduce_blocks() for GCD-based mesh reduction used during connectivity and periodicity matching.

__init__(X: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[_ScalarT]], Y: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[_ScalarT]], Z: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[_ScalarT]])[source]

Initialize a block from its coordinate arrays.

When the module-level flag plot3d.use_single_precision is set, coordinates are cast to float32; otherwise they remain as provided (typically float64).

Parameters:

  • X – 3-D array of X coordinates, shape (IMAX, JMAX, KMAX).

  • Y – 3-D array of Y coordinates, shape (IMAX, JMAX, KMAX).

  • Z – 3-D array of Z coordinates, shape (IMAX, JMAX, KMAX).

copy() → Block[source]

Return an independent deep copy of this block.

scale(factor: float)[source]

Uniformly scale all coordinates by a multiplicative factor.

Parameters:

factor – Scale factor applied to X, Y, and Z.

shift(shift_amount: float, direction: str = 'z')[source]

Translate the block along a single axis.

Parameters:

  • shift_amount – Distance to shift.

  • direction – Axis to shift along ('x', 'y', or 'z'). Defaults to 'z'.

cylindrical()[source]

Convert to cylindrical coordinates assuming X is the rotation axis.

Sets self.r (radius) and self.theta (azimuthal angle in radians) computed from Y and Z.

cell_volumes()[source]

Compute the volume of every hexahedral cell in the block.

Uses the method of Davies and Salmond (AIAA J., vol. 23, No. 6, pp. 954-956, 1985) which is exact for hexahedra whose faces are bilinear surfaces.

Returns:

Array of cell volumes with shape (IMAX, JMAX, KMAX). Volumes at boundary indices [0,:,:], [:,0,:], [:,:,0] are zero.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

get_faces()[source]

Return the six boundary face coordinate arrays.

Returns:

Keys are 'imin', 'imax', 'jmin', 'jmax', 'kmin', 'kmax'. Values are (X_face, Y_face, Z_face) tuples where each array is a 2-D slice of the block.

Return type:

dict

property size: int

Total number of nodes in the block (IMAX * JMAX * KMAX).

plot3d.block.compute_gcd(blocks: List[Block]) → int[source]

Compute the minimum GCD across all blocks’ dimensions.

For each block, computes gcd(IMAX-1, JMAX-1, KMAX-1) and returns the minimum. This shared factor is used by reduce_blocks() to down-sample every block uniformly before connectivity or periodicity matching, then scale results back up.

Parameters:

blocks – List of blocks to analyze.

Returns:

The minimum GCD factor (always >= 1).

plot3d.block.reduce_blocks(blocks: List[Block], factor: int)[source]

Down-sample blocks by subsampling every factor indices.

Each block’s X, Y, Z arrays are sliced with stride factor along all three axes, and IMAX, JMAX, KMAX are updated to reflect the new shape.

Warning

This modifies blocks in-place. Pass copies ([b.copy() for b in blocks]) if the originals must be preserved.

Parameters:

  • blocks – List of blocks to reduce. Modified in-place.

  • factor – Subsampling stride along each axis.

Returns:

The same list of blocks, now at reduced resolution.
